title: Some sterility in crosses between species is very general but not universal

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Some sterility in crosses between species is very general but not universal

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Some degree of sterility in first crosses between species and in their hybrids is an extremely general result, but it is not absolutely universal.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Finally, looking to all the ascertained facts on the intercrossing of plants and animals, it may be concluded that some degree of sterility, both in first crosses and in hybrids,is an extremely general result; but that it cannot, under our present state of knowledge, be considered as absolutely universal.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter VIII, “Hybridism”; section “Sterility various in degree, not universal, affected by close interbreeding, removed by domestication”. Scope: interspecific crosses in plants and animals

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch08-04: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.69

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Outcomes are measurable, but no complete public census of attempted crosses exists. Publication and experiment-selection biases prevent a secure estimate over plants and animals generally.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compile attempted interspecific crosses and estimate the frequency and degree of reduced F1 production and F1 fertility relative to within-species controls. High but non-unit prevalence supports the claim.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Failed and null crosses are underreported.

Available crosses are a highly selected taxonomic sample.

fields.value:

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The frequency claim has an obvious proportion, and one open dataset can estimate it inside Drosophila, including pairs fertile enough to challenge universality. Sampling bias and narrow taxonomy keep that from being a test of plants and animals generally. A broader compilation exists only as papers and would take months to harmonize.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Estimate the proportion of interspecific crosses with reduced fertility of the first cross or the hybrids, and ask whether any well-documented crosses are fully fertile. A high proportion plus at least some fully fertile exceptions would support 'extremely general but not universal'; either rarity of sterility or no fertile exceptions would count against that wording.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Taxonomic rank affects the denominator of 'between species'.

Published crosses favor tractable taxa and both unusually fertile and unusually sterile outcomes.

Drosophila does not stand in for plants and animals at large.
